ceiling_directive: Derive the packing-profile hypotheses from a primitive geometric density class—for example, densities controlled by transverse distance to a finite versus positive-length boundary zero set—and prove the same estimator rates uniformly on those classes.
improvement_directive: Strengthen the profile-adaptive estimator theorem by replacing the directly imposed isolated/pervasive packing envelopes with verifiable primitive score-density conditions and deriving the required mass and packing inequalities uniformly. This would turn the endpoint adaptation result into a broadly applicable boundary-design theorem rather than a result for bespoke profile classes.
critique: The delivered novelty is one estimator attaining two minimax rates whose converses and testing constructions are already attributed to the parent, plus a classical regular-design upper rate. The isolated and pervasive regimes are defined directly through the packing functional that drives the oracle penalty, while the note proves only one specially constructed density witness for each regime rather than a usable primitive characterization of designs satisfying those conditions. Thus the result is a technically substantial companion adaptation theorem, but it does not yet establish a new general frontier or a class practitioners can readily verify, and it supplies no application or numerical evidence showing the estimator's relevance. The framing accurately limits the claim to global-bandwidth endpoint adaptation and does not falsely claim local-oracle adaptation or confidence-band results. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
